meta.title: Oru: grow small. spread wide.
meta.description: Oru is a climate-habit game for India. Log small things you really did for waste, heat, energy and water, grow a pixel city, and wake your region's guardian animal.

hero.lead: Oru is a pocket game for India. Log the small things you really did for waste, heat, energy and water, grow a pixel city, and <u>wake the guardian animal</u> of your region.
hero.note: Free. Works on entry-level Android phones, even on a patchy connection.
hero.scene: An isometric plaza with Oru buddy in the middle, surrounded by six guardian habitats: a snowy mountain, dry grassland, a river, a wetland, a beach and a city block.

why.p1: Climate change, nature loss and pollution are linked problems. Scientists call them the triple planetary crisis.
why.p2: Big fixes need governments and industry, but everyday habits in homes and streets add up too. That is where Oru starts.

waste.name: Waste
waste.title: Sort it, reuse it, hand it over right
waste.body: Separate wet and dry waste, carry your own bag, and give recyclables to a kabadiwala.

heat.name: Heat
heat.title: Keep yourself and your street cooler
heat.body: Shade a window, water a street tree, and save the AC for when you need it.

energy.name: Energy
energy.title: Use less, switch cleaner
energy.body: Switch off at the plug, take the bus or metro, and ask about rooftop solar.

water.name: Water
water.title: Save it and keep it clean
water.body: Fix a dripping tap, reuse RO wastewater, and keep plastic out of drains.

day1.lead: Your first day takes <m>about a minute</m>.

step1.title: Log it
step1.body: Pick something you did today, like handing over sorted waste. Add a photo if you have one.

step2.title: Earn it
step2.body: Each action earns seeds. Actions checked with a photo or a QR scan <g>earn more</g> than a quick tap.

step3.title: Grow it
step3.body: Plant your seeds in your pixel city. Every tile you grow helps your guardian wake up.

day1.sampleNote: Example only. Real rewards depend on how the action is checked.

guardians.lead: Your guardian matches <g>the land where you live</g>. Turn a card over to read about it.

dolphin.name: River dolphin
dolphin.fact: The Ganges river dolphin is almost blind. It finds its way and its food in muddy water using sound. India named it the national aquatic animal in 2009.
dolphin.link: Less plastic and sewage in drains means cleaner rivers.

turtle.name: Sea turtle
turtle.fact: Olive ridley turtles can come ashore in large groups to nest on the same beach. Some of the biggest nesting beaches are on Odisha's coast.
turtle.link: Plastic and lost fishing nets are among the dangers they face at sea.

leopard.name: Snow leopard
leopard.fact: It lives high in the Himalaya, often above the tree line, and is so hard to spot that people call it the ghost of the mountains.
leopard.link: A warming climate is changing the snow and high pastures it depends on.

bustard.name: Great Indian bustard
bustard.fact: One of the heaviest flying birds, it lives in open dry grasslands, mostly in Rajasthan. Very few remain in the wild.
bustard.link: Collisions with overhead power lines are a major threat, so where new energy lines go matters.

sparrow.name: House sparrow
sparrow.fact: Once found around almost every home, it has become less common in many Indian cities. 20 March is World Sparrow Day.
sparrow.link: Trees, shade and green corners make hot streets kinder for birds and people.

crane.name: Sarus crane
crane.fact: It is the tallest flying bird in the world. Pairs are often seen together in the wetlands and farm fields of north India.
crane.link: It needs wetlands, so saving water and keeping ponds clean helps.

guardians.title: Six guardians, six kinds of land

growth.lead: Your pixel plot changes as your habits stick, and your guardian <u>wakes up a little more</u> at each stage.
growth.pace: The days are an example pace. Stages follow the actions you log, not the calendar.

seed.name: Seed
seed.body: Your first logged action plants a seed. Your guardian is fast asleep.

sprout.name: Sprout
sprout.body: A few days in, the first green shoots come up around it.

patch.name: Patch
patch.body: A week of small habits turns into a patch of green. Your guardian opens one eye.

grove.name: Grove
grove.body: Trees grow between new houses and a pond appears. Your guardian is awake and watching.

forest.name: Forest
forest.body: A month in, your plot is a small green city and your guardian is out exploring.

places.lead: Oru picks your guardian from <m>the land around you</m>. Choose a region to see who looks after it.
places.mapLabel: Simplified pixel map of India split into terrain regions
places.disclaimer: A simplified sketch for the game. Not to scale and not an official map of India.
places.pick: Choose a region on the map or in the list.

mountains.name: High mountains
mountains.body: The Himalaya and high valleys across the north.

dry.name: Deserts and dry grasslands
dry.body: The Thar desert in the west and the dry grasslands of the Deccan.

rivers.name: River plains
rivers.body: The wide plains of the Ganga and Brahmaputra and their many rivers.

wetlands.name: Wetlands and fields
wetlands.body: Lakes, marshes and farmland across the plains and central India.

coasts.name: Coasts and islands
coasts.body: Beaches, mangroves and islands along the east and west coasts.

cities.name: Cities
cities.body: Big and small cities everywhere, shown as dots on the map.

impact.lead: We only show numbers <m>we can stand behind</m>. Community totals start at zero and go live after launch.
impact.export: Your record is yours. Export every logged action as a JSON-LD file aligned with Mission LiFE, and take it wherever you like.
impact.estimate: Oru builds habits and estimates impact. It does not claim to save species or the planet.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.intro: Quick answers about playing Oru, your data, and getting started.

startWhat.a: A free pocket game for India. You log small things you really did for waste, heat, energy and water, grow a pixel city, and wake the guardian animal of your region.

startFree.q: Is it free, and does it work on older phones?
startFree.a: Yes. Oru is free and works on entry-level Android phones, even on a patchy connection.

startAccount.q: Do I need to make an account?
startAccount.a: No. There is no sign-up or login. Your language choice is saved only on this device.

missionsWhat.a: Four everyday categories to log actions in: Waste, Heat, Energy and Water. Each has simple, real things you can do, like sorting waste or fixing a dripping tap.

missionsSeeds.a: Seeds are what logged actions earn. Actions checked with a photo or a QR scan earn more seeds than a quick tap. You plant seeds in your pixel city to grow it.

missionsVerify.a: No. A quick tap still counts, it just earns fewer seeds than an action you back up with a photo or scan.

guardiansWhat.a: Oru picks a guardian animal for your region based on where you are. As your pixel city grows, your guardian wakes up a little more at each stage.

guardiansGrow.q: How does my pixel city grow?
guardiansGrow.a: It follows the actions you log, not the calendar. A logged action plants a seed; keep logging and it grows from a seed to a sprout, patch, grove and forest.

privacyData.a: Oru uses no cookies, no trackers and no third-party scripts. Your language choice is saved only on this device.

privacyExport.a: Yes. Your record is yours: you can export every logged action as a JSON-LD file aligned with Mission LiFE and take it wherever you like.

accessLang.a: English and Hindi at launch, with more planned.

accessA11y.a: We aim for WCAG 2.2 AA in both languages. If something does not work for you, tell us on GitHub.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Oru is built to need as little of your data as possible.
privacy.p1: Oru uses no cookies, no trackers and no third-party scripts. The only thing saved is your language choice, and that is kept on this device only, never sent to a server.
privacy.p2: When Oru launches, actions you log to play the game (and any photo you attach) are stored so your pixel city and guardian can reflect your progress. Your record is yours: you can export every logged action as a JSON-LD file aligned with Mission LiFE and take it wherever you like.
privacy.p3: There is no sign-up, no login and no advertising in Oru.
privacy.p4: If anything here is unclear, open an issue on GitHub and we will answer.

terms.title: Terms
terms.intro: Plain-language terms for a free, non-commercial game.
terms.p1: Log only things you really did. Oru's seeds and guardians are a game, not a currency; they cannot be bought, sold or exchanged for money.
terms.p2: Oru is provided as-is, built for a hackathon, with no guarantee it will be available at all times or free of bugs.
terms.p3: Any photo you choose to attach to a logged action stays yours. Do not upload anything that is not yours to share.
terms.p4: These terms may change as Oru develops. The current version always applies.
